newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia's Tudjman set for victory - partial result.
newsitem.headline: Croatia's Tudjman set for victory - partial result.

text.p: Croatian President Franjo Tudjman looks likely to sweep to victory in the presidential election with around two thirds of the votes counted, preliminary results broadcast on Croatian television showed on Monday.
First partial results showed Tudjman had won 59 percent. He needs to win 50 percent to avoid a second round run-off against an opposition candidate.
Zdravko Tomac of the Social Democratic party was in second place with 22.8 percent of the votes and Vlado Gotovac of the Croatian Social Liberal Party was in third place with 18.1 percent.
Head of the state electoral commission Ivan Mrkonjic said votes from 5,247 polling stations out of a total of 7,558 had been counted.
The two challengers faced an uphill battle to oust Tudjman, hailed as the "father of the nation" since he proclaimed independence for Croatia after its secession from federal Yugoslavia in 1991.
Tudjman is now set to come under increasing pressure from the United States and the West to tighten up his record on treatment of Serbs in Croatia and to loosen his grip on the state media.
